acceptance_criteria: `Kernel::shell(&self, s: &Self::Shape, open: &[SubShape], thickness: f64) -> Result<Self::Shape, KernelError>`, documented (walls grow inward from the original faces, so the outer size is unchanged) and implemented for `OcctKernel` with one new `noexcept` shim function that catches C++ exceptions and rejects a result `BRepCheck_Analyzer` finds invalid.

Box tests (behind `occt`), box 10 × 20 × 30 from the origin, volumes within a relative 1e-6, boxes within 1e-6: open the top face (z = 30), thickness 1: volume 6000 − 8·18·29 = 1824; bounding box (0, 0, 0)–(10, 20, 30); 11 faces. open the top and bottom faces, thickness 1: volume 30·(200 − 8·18) = 1680; 10 faces. the input solid is unchanged (volume 6000, 6 faces).
Cylinder test: `make_cylinder` radius 10, height 20 on +Z, open the top face, thickness 2: volume 2000π − 1152π = 848π ≈ 2664.0706 (relative 1e-6); bounding box unchanged.

Errors, each with a test and never a panic: an empty `open` list, a non-face `SubShape`, an index out of range, and a thickness that is zero, negative or not finite are `InvalidInput`, checked before the backend. Duplicate faces are accepted once. A thickness too large for the part (5 on the 10 × 20 × 30 box) is an error (`Backend` or `InvalidInput`), not a panic.

No new dependencies beyond an OCCT toolkit link. `swx-kernel` still has no workspace dependencies. Every new `unsafe` block is in `ffi` and documented; the algorithm's doc comment cites the OCCT reference documentation.
`cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace` pass, and so do the CI `swx-kernel (occt)` job commands.
QA report (FACTORY §6b) posted on the PR.
